Detect cholera outbreak onsets in a weekly case series

Source: R/calc_outbreak_onset.R
calc_outbreak_onset.Rd

Finds every outbreak in a weekly series of suspected cases and returns its onset, end and (in real time) detection week, by a growth-rate rule on a quasi-Poisson smooth (method = "growth"), the same rule with a lower bar for small outbreaks (method = "growth_sensitive"), or the Zheng et al. outbreak definition (method = "zheng"). Each rule runs either on the full series (mode = "retrospective") or one week at a time on the data known by that week (mode = "realtime"), which records the week an outbreak would have been declared. The growth rules work on the smooth by default (source = "smooth") or on growth rates and levels computed directly from the reported counts (source = "raw").

Usage

calc_outbreak_onset(
  cases,
  week_start,
  population,
  observed = !is.na(cases),
  method = c("growth", "growth_sensitive", "zheng"),
  mode = c("retrospective", "realtime"),
  source = c("smooth", "raw"),
  growth_min = 0.05,
  growth_z = 1.28,
  growth_weeks = 3L,
  floor_per100k = 0.05,
  min_size = 1.5,
  end_frac_peak = 0.5,
  end_run_weeks = 6L,
  merge_gap_weeks = 5L,
  realtime_start = 53L,
  raw_weeks = 2L,
  segment_weeks = 7.5,
  gcv_gamma = 1.4,
  lambda = 10^seq(-2, 5, by = 0.5)
)

Arguments

cases

Numeric vector of weekly suspected cases, one per consecutive week; values in unreported weeks are ignored.

week_start

Dates of the weeks' first days, consecutive 7 days apart.

population

Population, one value or one per week (used for the per-capita floor and the Zheng incidence).

observed

Logical vector, TRUE for reported weeks (default: non-missing cases).

method

"growth" (default), "growth_sensitive" or "zheng".

mode

"retrospective" (default, full series) or "realtime" (weekly step forward).

source

What the growth rules work on: "smooth" (default, the quasi-Poisson smooth) or "raw" (the reported counts; see Raw source). The Zheng rule always works on the counts.

growth_min

Minimum weekly growth of a growth week, as a proportion (0.05 = 5% a week).

growth_z

Multiple of the growth standard error that r must exceed (1.28: lower 80% bound > 0; 0.84 for "growth_sensitive"); 0 drops the check.

growth_weeks

Consecutive growth weeks that start an outbreak in the full series (real time uses its own three-week rule).

floor_per100k

Floor on the threshold, in suspected cases per 100,000 per week (0.05; 0.02 for "growth_sensitive").

min_size

An outbreak's smoothed peak must reach this multiple of the threshold.

end_frac_peak

A week below this fraction of the outbreak's running peak is low.

end_run_weeks

Number of consecutive low weeks that end an outbreak (growth rule).

merge_gap_weeks

A start within this many weeks of the previous end continues that outbreak.

realtime_start

Week number, from the first reported week, of the first real-time estimate.

raw_weeks

With source = "raw": weeks in each of the two consecutive totals whose ratio gives the growth rate, and in the trailing mean that gives the level.

segment_weeks

Width of a B-spline segment, in weeks.

gcv_gamma

Inflation of the effective degrees of freedom in the GCV score.

lambda

Grid of smoothing parameters searched by GCV.

Value

A data frame with one row per outbreak (zero rows when there is none):

outbreak_id

1, 2, ... in onset order.

onset_week

First week of the outbreak.

detection_week

Week the outbreak was declared (real time); NA retrospectively.

peak_week, peak_cases

Week and count of the largest reported weekly count in the outbreak.

peak_smoothed

Largest smoothed mean over the outbreak's reported weeks (in real time, of the newest estimates; with source = "raw", the largest level); NA for the Zheng rule.

end_week

Last week of the outbreak; NA while it is still open at the end of the series.

complete

FALSE when the outbreak is still open at the last reported week (for the Zheng rule, also when it closes only inside the trailing padding).

left_censored

TRUE when the onset is the first analysed week or follows an unreported week, so the outbreak may have begun earlier.

duration_weeks, total_cases

Weeks and reported cases from onset to end (or to the last reported week).

threshold_cases, threshold_per100k

The level threshold at the onset week (real time: at the detection week), in cases per week and per 100,000 per week.

method, mode

As called.

source

What the rule worked on: "smooth" or "raw" (always "raw" for the Zheng rule).

The attribute "series" is a data frame with one row per analysed week: week_start, cases, observed, mu (smoothed mean; in real time the newest estimate at each week), r, r_lo, r_hi (growth rate and its 95% interval), threshold (cases per week) and in_outbreak. The smooth columns are NA for the Zheng rule. Over unreported weeks they interpolate or extrapolate the spline with no data there and can be far off over a long gap; the rules use them only at reported weeks, so plot them on reported weeks only. With source = "raw", mu is the level and r the raw growth rate (see Raw source), NA at unreported weeks and, for r, wherever its 2 x raw_weeks weeks are not all reported.

Details

The series is analysed from its first to its last reported week; week numbers below count from the first reported week.

Growth rule (the "tuned2" settings of the onset-detection handoff of 18 November 2026). The series is smoothed by a quasi-Poisson P-spline: cubic B-splines on segments of segment_weeks weeks from the first analysed week, a second-order difference penalty, and the smoothing parameter chosen by GCV (with gcv_gamma) over lambda; unreported weeks are left out of the fit. This gives the smoothed mean mu and the weekly growth rate r = d log(mu) / dt with its standard error. The level threshold is max(B, floor), where the floor is floor_per100k cases per 100,000 per week and B is the mean of mu over reported weeks outside outbreaks, iterated with the outbreak set until it repeats (at most 25 rounds). An outbreak starts at a reported week where mu is at or above the threshold and the next growth_weeks weeks (that week included) are reported growth weeks: r >= log(1 + growth_min) and r - growth_z x se > 0. A week is low when unreported or when mu is below max(threshold, end_frac_peak x the outbreak's running peak); end_run_weeks consecutive low weeks end the outbreak at the second of them. A start within merge_gap_weeks of that end continues the same outbreak, still judged against its earlier peak. An outbreak whose smoothed peak stays below min_size x the threshold is discarded.

In real time the smooth is refitted at every week T from week realtime_start on the reported weeks up to T (warm-started from the previous week's fit). Because the segments have a fixed width, each fit uses only the data known at T: the result up to T is the same whether or not the series continues. Week T - 2 becomes a candidate at T (so the first decision is at week realtime_start + 1) when weeks T - 2 to T are reported, its smoothed level is at or above the threshold, and the growth condition holds at T - 1 and T in fit T and at T - 2 and T - 1 in fit T - 1; this three-week condition replaces growth_weeks. The candidate is declared at the first reported week whose newest smoothed estimate reaches min_size x the threshold (the detection week), and dropped if it ends first. The real-time threshold is a different statistic from the retrospective one: max(mean of the counts to date outside declared outbreaks, unreported weeks counted as zero, floor). An outbreak ends as in the full series, but its running peak restarts at an end, so a merged continuation is judged against its own peak.

Sensitive growth rule (method = "growth_sensitive"). The growth rule, in both modes, with two defaults changed, for small outbreaks in large populations: floor_per100k = 0.02, so the threshold can fall to the series' own baseline (a 0.05 floor is about 29 cases a week in Kenya, above its baseline of about 15), and growth_z = 0.84, so a growth week needs the lower 60% bound of r above zero instead of the lower 80% bound. Arguments given explicitly override these defaults. On the 40 MOSAIC countries it finds every outbreak of the growth rule plus smaller ones, such as Kenya's 2024-2025 waves of 46-70 cases a week, and dates some shared onsets earlier; it also raises more outbreaks in sparse or blocky noise.

Raw source (source = "raw"). The growth rules, in both modes and with the same settings, on quantities computed from the reported counts instead of the smooth, with k = raw_weeks: the level at week t is the mean of the reported counts among the k weeks ending at t; the growth rate r is log((S_t + 0.5) / (S_t-k + 0.5)) / k, where S_t is the total of the k weeks ending at t; and its standard error is the Poisson one, sqrt(1 / (S_t + 0.5) + 1 / (S_t-k + 0.5)) / k. A week has no growth rate unless all 2k weeks are reported. The windows trail, so a rise registers about (k - 1) / 2 weeks later than in the smooth. Nothing is refitted, so real time takes no longer than the full series, and in real time a candidate needs three consecutive growth weeks (T - 2, T - 1 and T). segment_weeks, gcv_gamma and lambda do not apply. On the 40 MOSAIC countries (imputed days unreported) the raw growth rule with raw_weeks = 2 finds 90 outbreaks in the full series against the smooth's 85, 53 of them within 4 weeks of a smooth onset; in real time 82 against 81 (50 matched, detected a median of one week later). With raw_weeks = 1 it finds only 37 (20 matched): a single dip breaks a run of rising weeks. In outbreak-free series it raises false outbreaks where the counts are over-dispersed, because its Poisson standard error ignores that (see Caveats).

Zheng rule (Zheng et al. 2022, Int J Infect Dis 122:215-221; as implemented in OutbreakExtractR, HopkinsIDD, main @ 4fcdc21). Eight zero weeks pad the series before its first and after its last reported week, and unreported weeks count as zero. The threshold is the mean weekly incidence, sum(cases / population) / (weeks - 1). A week is high when its incidence is at or above the threshold with cases > 0. An outbreak starts at a high week followed by two strict increases in the counts (only when at least three weeks are high), and ends the week after the first week that begins a run of at least six low weeks; a start at or before that end belongs to the same outbreak. In real time the threshold at week T uses the weeks up to T and the eight leading padding weeks, week T - 2 is declared at T, and an outbreak ends at the second of six consecutive weeks that are not high. The growth-rule arguments do not apply.

Caveats.

  • GCV usually selects the smallest lambda of the grid, so the knots (their width and position) set most of the smoothing, and shifting them moves growth onsets: 7.5-week segments reproduce 45 of the handoff's 96 onsets exactly and 75 within two weeks.

  • The dispersion estimate collapses in very sparse series (mostly zeros), which shrinks the growth standard error; there only the floor guards against small rises.

  • With source = "raw", the growth standard error is Poisson's, which ignores the over-dispersion of reported counts. In outbreak-free negative binomial series of 10-50 cases a week it raises 4-10 false outbreaks per 10 years with raw_weeks = 2 (17 with 3), where the smooth raises none; raising growth_z barely helps (6 at growth_z = 3). In Poisson noise it raises almost none. The settings were chosen on the smooth.

  • The real-time 95% growth intervals at the newest week under-cover.

  • A reporting gap of seven or more weeks always ends an outbreak.

  • An onset at the first analysed week or just after an unreported week (left_censored) may have begun earlier.

See also

est_outbreak_onsets to run every location of a MOSAIC config.

Examples

weeks <- seq(as.Date("2020-01-06"), by = 7, length.out = 160)
lambda_t <- 5 + 400 * exp(-((seq_along(weeks) - 100) / 6)^2)
set.seed(1)
x <- calc_outbreak_onset(rpois(160, lambda_t), weeks, population = 1e6)
x[, c("onset_week", "end_week", "peak_cases")]
#>   onset_week   end_week peak_cases
#> 1 2021-08-23 2022-01-10        402
